summary: Ram Chandra Kak was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Sri Pratap College (~1909–1913) and under John Marshall (1914–1919). He served as superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1914–1918) and headed archaeology and research in Jammu and Kashmir (1919–1930).

An Indologist working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ram Chandra Pandeya studied under T. R. V. Murti (~1955–1958) and Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (~1959–1963). He served at the University of Delhi as Professor and Department Head of Buddhist Studies (~1969–1974) and Acharya (~1974–1996).

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Patna University and the University of California, Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau (PhD ~1956–1959), he served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Active in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Ram Mohan Roy founded several institutions, including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), the Calcutta Unitarian Committee, and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, completing his doctoral studies under supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Prasad Bhatt works in Indology and linguistics. He completed doctoral studies at Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (2003–2006) and held posts as Lecturer/Research Associate at the University of Leipzig (2002–2003) and Senior Lecturer/Research Associate at the University of Hamburg (2003).

Active in Indology and philosophy, Ram Shankar Bhattacharya studied under Raghunatha Shastri. He served as an अध्यापक at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and as an अनुसन्धानसहायक at both Banaras Hindu University and the All-India Kashiraj Trust.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was an Indologist working in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He headed Buddhist philosophy departments at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1973–1994) and served as Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1994–2004).

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian-archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Patna University, Patna College, and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and Wilhelm Rau. He headed history departments at Patna University (1958–1973) and the University of Delhi (1973–1978).
Rama Kant Agnihotri is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at York University (1973–1975, DPhil 1979) and served on the editorial board at the University of Delhi from 1980 to 2010.

Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested as a Professor (1882–1889) and as an Assistant Professor of Sāṅkhya (1914).

Rama Nath Sharma is a linguist and Indologist who studied at BHU, Allahabad, Agra, and the University of Rochester (PhD ~1968–1971). He held teaching posts at Allahabad (1962–1966), Rochester (1971–1976), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1976).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen (PhD 1885). He was a professor at Elphinstone and Deccan College, and served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramanath Pandey is an Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University, Delhi University, and Ranchi University (PhD 1984–1989). He served as a Research Associate at Delhi University, a Research Officer at Baroda (2004–2022), and became Professor at Parshwanath Vidyapeeth in 2025.

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist who served in the Sādhulāla Research Department at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and later served as Head of the Veda Department at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He lectured at the University of Calcutta (1920–1921), served as Superintendent at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (1921–1932), and founded the Varendra Research Museum.
Ramaprasada Tripathi is a scholar in Indology and linguistics whose affiliation with Sampurnanand Sanskrit University is attested in 1976 and 2001.

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who earned his BA and PhD at Calcutta University and a DLitt at Jadavpur University. He served as Vice Chancellor of Burdwan University (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati University (~1984–1987), and Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (~2002–2007).
Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indology scholar attested in 1891 as an Assistant Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as an अध्यापक at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Samskrta at Gujarat Vidyapith and held professorships of Sanskrit at L. D. Arts College and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (both attested 1938).
